edge_explainer: Lightwave Logic carries a one-billion-dollar market capitalisation on two hundred forty-three thousand dollars of trailing revenue — roughly four thousand three hundred times sales. The screen flagged it for a 98% gross margin and a 142% three-year revenue growth rate; both are computed off approximately nothing, which is the actual finding: our own gates have no revenue-materiality floor and will fire on any pre-commercial company. The business model is visible in the share count, which went from 129 million to 154 million in nine months while cash jumped forty million dollars in the December quarter — a burn of roughly twenty million a year funded by issuing stock into every rally, with a four-thousand-times-sales multiple as the collateral. Cash per share is forty-nine cents against a $6.82 price, so there is no floor within 93% of here. The polymer modulator research may well be real; that is not the question. The question is whether a billion dollars is a defensible price for an option that has produced a quarter of a million dollars of cumulative revenue, and no primary source supports it — which is exactly why it trades on attention and why the house neither buys it nor shorts it.
